title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LAMONT'S BIG KITE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lamont Gaskins of Port Aransas, Texas.
Thirty-four years running a refinery boiler. Then he retired.
Three weeks later, his wife Gloria caught him sorting her spice rack. Again.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE OCTOPUS
segments.author: Joseph Campbell
lines: Gloria sent him to the beach. There he saw a forty-foot purple octopus. Flying.
Holding the string was Teodoro, eighty-two, grinning ear to ear.
Lamont said, I don't know what to do with myself. Teodoro quoted the writer Joseph Campbell:
Follow your bliss.
That afternoon Lamont bought sticks, string and a cheap shower curtain.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE WIND
segments.quote: If you are looking for perfect safety, you will do well to sit on a fence and watch the birds.
segments.author: Wilbur Wright
lines: His shower curtain kite was beautiful. But he only flew it on calm days, so it never went up.
Teodoro said the Wright brothers learned on kites, and quoted Wilbur Wright:
If you are looking for perfect safety, you will do well to sit on a fence and watch the birds.
So Lamont went out on a windy day. The kite climbed so fast he yelled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TWO PAIRS OF HANDS
segments.quote: What is a friend? A single soul dwelling in two bodies.
segments.author: Aristotle
lines: Next he dreamed bigger. A thirty-foot redfish. But he could not sew a straight line.
Gloria walked into the garage, took the needle, and said, Move over.
She quoted the Greek thinker Aristotle:
What is a friend? A single soul dwelling in two bodies.
Forty years married, they built that fish together, arguing about every fin.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: FESTIVAL MORNING
segments.quote: The secret of success in life is for a man to be ready for his opportunity when it comes.
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: Then came the big kite festival. The forecast said no wind, and half the flyers went to breakfast.
Lamont remembered the British leader Benjamin Disraeli:
The secret of success in life is for a man to be ready for his opportunity when it comes.
So he stayed, lines untangled. At ten fifteen a breeze came. His fish was first up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TANGLE
segments.quote: Nothing gives one person so great advantage over another, as to remain always cool and unruffled under all circumstances.
segments.author: Thomas Jefferson
lines: Then a man's giant dragon crossed his line. The two kites wrapped up like a pretzel.
The man started yelling. Lamont thought of Thomas Jefferson:
Nothing gives one person so great advantage over another, as to remain always cool and unruffled under all circumstances.
So Lamont laughed and untangled it, knot by knot. By noon the dragon man bought him a lemonade.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: NEXT YEAR
segments.quote: My interest is in the future because I'm going to spend the rest of my life there.
segments.author: Charles Kettering
lines: A reporter asked, Why start something new at sixty-one?
Lamont quoted the inventor Charles Kettering:
My interest is in the future because I'm going to spend the rest of my life there.
Then he and Gloria signed up for next year.
And her spice rack is safe.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Find your joy. Fly in real wind. Build it together. Be ready. Stay cool. Look ahead.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Find your joy. Fly in real wind. Build it together. Be ready. Stay cool. And look ahead.
I flew a kite once. It landed in a tree, and so did my hat.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
